title: Why does a planner have a subscription fee?
body: The product looks great, and I have major ADHD, and want a tool that will better help me to organize my day-to-day life than apps like Google Keep/Tasks, which don’t have very much functionality beyond basic note taking and check-list creation. That said, I can’t justify spending $6/month on a planner app. If you go and buy a paper-based organizer you don’t go back to the store and pay $6 every month. I could maybe agree with a small annual fee, but beyond a one time charge, I find it aggravating that app-developers squeeze consumers for monthly payments on such simple products. I would have no problem paying $20 for the product. There is no way that you need to charge $6 to both make a profit, and maintain the app - it’s a planner, not helping me to split the atom.

title: Addictive & Genuinely Useful
body:
I’ve been really loving Lunatask for the past few weeks and, while initially downloaded just to play with it, I’ll be sticking with it for the long haul. The UI (desktop and phone) is clean but still pops enough to be engaging, its approach to task management is bizarrely fresh feeling, and the app in general is rather addictive to use. Best of all? I’m actually getting heaps of work done with it and enjoying peace of mind for having things all in one place. 

I love how everything’s brought together. Usually a task app trying to be a habit tracker and a note taker and a timeboxer etc just ends up being a UI hot mess that’s suboptimal at all of these functions. Lunatask nails the combo with grace. 

I was especially surprised by the usefulness of the notes and trackers. If you can get by with simple notes apps like Bear, Lunatask will have you covered. The mood, energy, and stress tracking has been shockingly useful. It’s been interesting seeing which emotion tags come up often and how they shift over time - patterns between those and energy levels and tasks completed show up pretty quickly. Planning what work to stick into Now around anticipated energy has potential. 

Overall, Lunatask feels well thought out and is actually super helpful, not just another productivity tool to play with for a bit before replacing.

Huge thanks to the Lunatask team for such a thoughtful tool!! And extra bonus points for nailing productivity so uniquely in such a crowded market. :)

title: Thoughtful Productivity App
body: Lunatask is the most thoughtful and intentional productivity app that I’ve come across yet. It takes task management to the next level by organizing tasks how they often come to us — in the context of a goal serving an Area of Life (aka Area of Focus in other productivity frameworks). That’s in addition to the many mundane spontaneous to-dos that pop up in everyday life. The thoughtful integration of practical Habit, Mood, Energy, and Emotion tracking features and the UX makes it more likely to actually use those features in a way that benefits you IRL. Don’t forget Notes and Journaling with the ability to keep everything worth remembering in context using backlinks and regular old hyperlinks. The documentation is fantastic. It makes getting the most out of the app nearly effortless. Tons of great productivity advice too. That reminds me of the ability to switch to any of several incredibly effective workflows at anytime. These go way beyond simple prioritization. The author can be proud of this work. I can tell there will be more great features to come. You can even contribute ideas!

title: Love this app!
body:
The task prioritization options are phenomenal. I did subscribe to access the Eisenhower Matrix, which is my favorite. Sometimes I feel the need to switch it up a bit so I will look at how my tasks look in other formats such as Do Now/Do Later. I like that each goal/life area can use a different prioritization system.
Don’t use notes much yet.
The habit tracker and mood tracker are great! I think my favorite part about them is that the mood tracker allows you to select multiple emotions. You don’t have to sum a day up in one word. Days can be complex. I won’t use a one-word mood tracker. The corresponding smiley is highlighted in multiple mood colors to match! This makes me happy every time I log my mood - to see the range of emotion areas.
The journal is convenient and I like that it’s secured with a pin. The Happy Memories entries help boost my mental health, and really call out the highlights of my life as I scroll back through the journal.
I like the personal CRM a lot! I document interactions/conversations, and am testing out the ‘reconnect by x’ feature. This is a great feature to have while disconnecting from social media platforms. I get to control how often I want to see/interact with others, instead of having an algorithm trying to decide for me. I didn’t even realize I needed this. Thank you!

It’s not perfect. It lacks in some filterability. It doesn’t do projects great (not a big for me with my personal productivity, I just link to project boards or wherever as needed) or dependencies (but I don’t think that’s its goal). And I think the pinned features is misguided in its current state, it can’t pin tasks across Areas. I’d give it 5 stars if it offered a way to pin or somehow prioritize tasks across areas.

But it works well enough, better than all others.

title: By far the best to do app I’ve used (and I’ve used most all)
body:
Underrated app by far. I’ve inserted it into my primary toolkit. It’s not perfect, but I find most to do apps severely lacking in terms of how I think of and prefer to organize my work. I love working in Areas and Goals/Projects, even had my own to do database set up in Notion which followed the same ideas. But Lunatask gave me a better experience to work in. And one of the simple beauties is each Area can support any flavor or work style, whether you prefer to use GTD (now/later), Kanban, Eisenhower, must/should/want, simple priority list, and other flavors, it supports them all! And each area can run a different flavor! And despite that robust capability, it’s beautifully simple. And as a keyboard power user on desktop I am grateful they support most features with simple hotkeys (and everything else with a power search at least on desktop).

It is lacking in some ability to filter and find stuff, but it supports enough to get by. And there certainly are other features that could be added, other nice to haves, but they’ve got a great foundation at least so far as user experience, and whatever they add I hope they things simple moving forward. 

I’ve looked far and wide for a to do app I can tolerate, and I’ve seriously considered many times writing my own because everything I’ve used (including my custom notion database) is lacking in something important to me. But thankfully Lunatask spared me from having to do so, I’m on board with no plans to switch.

Thanks Lunatask team! Keep up the great work!
author: thezimmee

title: A real game-changer
body:
I’ve been through a ton of tasking apps, from ToDoist to Amazing Marvin to a paper bullet journal and beyond. This one succeeds where they all fail: it’s simple, it’s elegant, it doesn’t take ten years of setting up, and it automatically surfaces the stuff you should probably be doing next. 

Best of all, the developer is super responsive to feedback and suggestions. Could not recommend Lunatask more highly.

author: lr00429

title: I LOVE IT
body:
I am a senior in high school, have severe ADHD, and have had so much trouble with organization in the past, but this app is a game changer! I am still on the free version of the app, but am considering paying for premium, as I already love the app so much!! I love how you can create good AND bad habits to track. I also LOVE how you can drag your tasks into the calendar and change the amount of time spent on them. It helps me to not be as overwhelmed when starting work. I also love how you can track your mood and put notes in for the day!!

Suggestions: 
-I think having a calendar that extends into the future so you can add in scheduled appointments in the future could be really helpful
-Adding more moods such as stressed, tired, unproductive, motivated, and excited could be really fun instead of just having emotions on a range from happy to sad
-Making it so that when you have checkboxes for sub-tasks in the notes of tasks, if you check one or more of the boxes, it changed the status to in progress or shows the percentage of completion or something

I LOVE THIS APP
